title: Training Notes: Late Vehicle Inspections and Inspection Validity on Wayfare Agreements
content:
These notes cover a rule of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product: a Wayfare driver's record of late vehicle inspections shortens the inspection validity days, the calendar days from the inspection date for which a passed vehicle inspection counts as the vehicle inspection on file.

**Rule.** When the standing record holds three or more second expiry notices for the vehicle inspection dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the recording day, the inspection validity days change by -20 days; when it holds one or two, they change by -10 days; when it holds none, they do not change.

| Second expiry notices for the vehicle inspection, dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the recording day | Change |
|---|---|
| three or more | -20 |
| one or two | -10 |
| none | 0 |

### Questions answered

**Which notices?** Second expiry notices sent for the vehicle inspection. First notices, and notices for other documents, are not counted.

**Which day is the window measured from?** The recording day, the day support records the inspection.

**Hypothetical example.** Recording day 2026-03-10. Second notices for the vehicle inspection dated 2024-02-20, 2025-02-21 and 2026-02-20: the notice of 2024-02-20 is more than 24 whole calendar months back, two count, and the change is -10.
